title: Compact AML hackpad: quant + prompt quick-runs
content:
Purpose:
- Rapid, cramped scratchpad for a few compact evals: try 4-bit quantization on 2 candidate models and baseline float16. Focus: small prompt-regression, hallucination surface, one-shot Q/A style. Keep logs terse for quick iteration.

Context / goals:
- Product asks: shipping-friendly model that keeps p95 < 300ms for short prompts (<= 64 tokens) and unit cost < $0.0006/token on Dedicated pool.
- Candidate models: redwood-v1-mini (7B), redwood-micro-13B (13B).
- Hypothesis: 4-bit GPTQ-like quant on v1-mini will hit latency/cost targets with minimal quality loss for our FAQ-style workload; 13B compressed may still be too expensive.

Quick checklist before running:
- [ ] sync weights from s3 (s3://redwood-models/staging/) -> local temp cache
- [ ] ensure kernels fallback for Triton path: set ENV TRITON_OPT=1 for quick profile
- [ ] dataset: /s3/redwood-evals/faq-shot-1.jsonl (1000 queries)
- [ ] regen prompts folder: prompts/faq-one-shot-v2.txt (see prompt enumerations below)
- [ ] start a short duration traffic generator for p95 profiling (wrk with 8 threads, 50 connections)

Prompt sets (compact) - local file: prompts/faq-one-shot-v2.txt\- prompt_A: "You are a docs assistant. Answer concisely. Q: {question}\nA:"
- prompt_B: same as A but add "If unknown, say 'I don't know.'"
- prompt_C: add system context with product name and example answer style (1 example)

Experiment matrix (quick):
1) v1-mini float16 baseline (run id: evelyn_run_20250803_f16)
- quant: none
- batch size: 8 (default)
- backend: cuda-fused kernels (profiled)
- notes: warmup 200 queries
2) v1-mini 4-bit GPTQ-ish (run id: evelyn_run_20250804_q4)
- quant: 4-bit, per-channel, outlier handling enabled
- reorder KV caching disabled (temp to test correctness)
- fast path: int8 fallback on some ops
3) micro-13B 4-bit (run id: evelyn_run_20250805_13b_q4)
- quant: 4-bit, compression aggressive
- batch size: 4 for latency target

Run details & quick logs:
- evelyn_run_20250803_f16:
  - start: 2025-08-03T09:10
  - dataset: faq-shot-1.jsonl (n=1000)
  - p50/p95/p99 single token time observed (~ms): 18 / 230 / 320
  - mean tokens per response: 24
  - obvious failure mode: safe-bias on vendor-name questions (overly verbose)
  - qualitative: prompt_B reduced hallucination but increased token length ~+2 tokens

- evelyn_run_20250804_q4:
  - start: 2025-08-04T11:05
  - p50/p95/p99: 12 / 180 / 260  (note: lower across the board vs f16)
  - memory: stable; GPU mem saved ~42% vs f16 baseline
  - quality: BLEU-ish quick metric dropped ~0.9% absolute; factuality regression on 7/100 sampled Qs (contradiction/omission)
  - weird: on Q "How to rotate API key?" model injected slightly different command syntax ("redwood keys rotate") - flag as safe regression

- evelyn_run_20250805_13b_q4:
  - start: 2025-08-05T14:20
  - p50/p95/p99: 28 / 340 / 480 (too slow for p95 target)
  - cost est: ~2.7x v1-mini per token; quant reduced but still > target
  - notes: occasional OOM when batch=6, even with kv cache trimmed

Quick micro-observations (manual spot checks):
- prompt_C improved instruction-following on multi-step answers but added ~4 tokens avg. Good for support multistep flows, not for short-faq use-case.
- 4-bit instantiation tends to mute very rare tokens -> slightly hollowed style on code-like answers (missing backticks); maybe due to outlier handling threshold.

Immediate TODOs (prioritized):
1) Fix: reproduce the "rotate API key" hallucination with deterministic seed, add failing sample to regression set (owner: Evelyn, ETA: 2 days).
2) Run controlled ablation: per-channel vs per-tensor quant, compare same v1-mini (owner: Liam, ETA: 4 days).
3) Add a short-run with prompt_C + 4-bit but with KV cache enabled to check style retention (owner: Sofia, ETA: 3 days).
4) Add perf smoke on Dedicated pool with autoscale=off to capture true p95 under reserved capacity (owner: Evelyn, ETA: next week).

Open questions / discussion notes:
- Is the factuality regression correlated with specific layers being quantized? Need layerwise error heatmap. Hypothesis: early MLP layers show more token-drift when quantized aggressively.
- For product, is a small factuality increase tolerable if latency and cost targets are met? Scoped proposal: allow up to 2% factuality regression on FAQ-only traffic if can meet p95 < 250ms and cost < $0.0006/token.
- Are there legal/compliance concerns if model gives slightly wrong instructions for security actions (key rotation)? Escalate to security team if regression persists.

Notes-to-self (short commands):
- quick local eval: python scripts/run_eval.py --model v1-mini-q4 --prompts prompts/faq-one-shot-v2.txt --out logs/v1mini_q4_eval.jsonl --limit 200
- dump sample: jq 'select(.answer | length>0) | {q:.question, a:.answer}' logs/v1mini_q4_eval.jsonl | head -n 40 > tmp/sample-check.json

Back-of-envelope numbers (per-token):
- v1-mini f16: $0.0009/token (dedicated amortized)
- v1-mini q4: ~$0.00045/token
- micro-13B q4: ~$0.0012/token

Reference links:
- TODO: add confluence link to quantization doc (placeholder)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rlhf-experiments/pull/231 (contains quant scripts)

Session end notes:
- Early signal: v1-mini q4 looks promising for FAQ vertical if we can fix 7% of sampled factual regressions via prompt engineering or selective layer exceptions.
- Keep this doc tight; move polished findings to Confluence when we have solid regression tests and A/B plan.

-- Evelyn
